sections.content: You know *es importante que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. Here you evaluate choices with *es mejor*, *es preferible*, *es conveniente* and *merece la pena*. Use an infinitive when no one in particular is named, and *que* + subjunctive when someone is.

items.spanish: Es mejor esperar antes de decidir.
items.english: It is better to wait before deciding.

items.spanish: Es preferible elegir una opción más segura.
items.english: It is preferable to choose a safer option.

items.spanish: Es conveniente que revisemos los costes.
items.english: It is advisable that we review the costs.

items.spanish: Creo que merece la pena aceptar el riesgo.
items.english: I think it is worth accepting the risk.

sections.content: Remember: *es conveniente que revisemos* takes the subjunctive because it names who should act (*nosotros*); *es mejor esperar* and *es preferible elegir* stay in the infinitive because no one in particular is named.
